$comment: L0 reference layer. Two DIFFERENT kinds of number live here and must not be conflated: (a) population requirements - what an average adult needs to avoid inadequacy, sourced from ICMR-NIN because this is an India-first product; (b) upper limits - the ceiling the dose ledger checks a stacked total against, sourced from IOM/NIH ODS and FDA because ICMR-NIN does not publish a comparable full UL set. Goal-adjusted targets (e.g. 1.6-2.2 g/kg protein for a lifter) are NOT requirements and do not belong here - they are expert policy and live in policy/dosing/.

sources.name: ICMR-NIN, Nutrient Requirements for Indians: Recommended Dietary Allowances and Estimated Average Requirements
Institute of Medicine Dietary Reference Intakes, tolerable upper intake levels (as summarised by NIH Office of Dietary Supplements)
US FDA guidance on EPA and DHA intake from supplements

_todo: WORK PACKAGE A4. The `requirements` array below is intentionally near-empty rather than filled with plausible-looking numbers. Populate it from the ICMR-NIN 2020 report (source key ICMR-NIN-2020), one row per compound per age/sex band, using RDA where published and EAR where the gap assessment needs it. Nothing in the engine reads a requirement row today except protein, so this does not block the build - but every micronutrient gap assessment stays disabled until it is done. Do not substitute US DRI values for Indian RDAs without flagging it: they differ, and the whole point of an India-first product is that this table is Indian.

requirements.note: Baseline adequacy for a sedentary adult. NOT the target for someone training - that is a goal-adjusted target and lives in policy/dosing/dose-protein-resistance-training.json, sourced from the ISSN position stand. Keeping the two apart is deliberate: one is a population requirement, the other is our expert-signed policy.

upperLimit.note: PREFORMED retinol only. Beta-carotene is not counted against this ceiling - a ledger that treats them alike will raise false alarms.
Applies to synthetic folic acid from supplements and fortified food, not to food folate.
Adults. Lower thresholds apply in haemochromatosis - handled as a safety escalation, not as a ledger limit.
Adults 19-50. Drops to 2000 mg/day at 51+ - the ledger must read the age band, not a single figure.
SUPPLEMENTAL magnesium only. Food magnesium is not counted against this.

Conservative engine ceiling. FDA advises no more than 2 g/day from supplements and 3 g/day total; EFSA concluded supplemental intakes up to 5 g/day raise no safety concern. The engine uses the tighter figure and escalates above it rather than picking a side. FLAGGED FOR EXPERT REVIEW - this is a judgment call between two authorities, not a settled number.

upperLimits.note: No UL established (low toxicity). Absence of a UL is recorded explicitly so the ledger distinguishes 'no limit' from 'limit not yet entered'.
No UL established. Doses up to 30 g/day have been studied over multi-year periods without evidence of harm in healthy adults; the engine still recommends only the standard 3-5 g/day maintenance dose.
No UL established for healthy adults with normal renal function. Sustained intake above ~2.2 g/kg/day without medical guidance is handled as a caution in dosing policy, not as a hard ceiling.
